allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A blind concert violinist gets a cornea transplant allowing her to see again. However, she gets more than she bargained for when she realizes her new eye can see ghosts. She sets out to find the origins of the cornea and discover the fate of its former host.

facts.director: Oxide Pang Chun & Danny Pang Phat

facts.title: The Eye

semanticBoundaryFlags.message: The packet does not ground social viewing contexts such as date-night or friends; only alone is evidenced, so additional situations should be reviewed before adding.
Suspenseful and emotional are both grounded, but the horror packet leaves relaxing/funny clearly unsupported; confirm no third mood is intended on review.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Her new vision was supposed to restore her life, but whose terrifying memories are lingering behind her eyes?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After receiving a cornea transplant to regain her sight, a blind violinist begins seeing restless spirits, driving her to uncover the history of the organ and the fate of its former host.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A steady, suspenseful horror that balances ghostly unease with an engaging, tragic mystery best experienced alone.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Oxide and Danny Pang, this cross-regional Asian horror combines chilling supernatural imagery with an emotionally grounded search for truth.
